case_name: M57 Patents / DFRWS 2009 — Network Capture Identity Attribution (July 2008)
carnegie_pattern_expected: Dual identity concealment (personal Gmail + corporate AIM on same LAN)
description: Network packet capture (nitroba.pcap, 56180821 bytes, SHA-256: 2b77a9eaefc1d6af163d1ba793c96dbccacb04e6befdf1a0b01f8c67553ec2fb) from the M57 Patents DFRWS 2009 forensics challenge. Capture period: July 21-22, 2008. The packet capture contains traffic from a residential LAN with two identified devices: (1) 192.168.1.64 — Mac OS X 10.5.4 (both PPC and Intel variants seen), running Safari 3.1.2 and Firefox 2.0.0.16. User logged into Gmail as mylady.ixchel@gmail.com, then logged out. Reading BBC News RSS (July 21, 2008) and PHD Comics (academic webcomic about graduate students). Screen 1920x1200, Flash 9.0.124. (2) 192.168.15.4 — Windows XP SP2 (NT 5.1.0.2600), running AOL AIM client v4.1.4.1. Performing SyncML contact synchronization for account 'm57jean' with AOL servers (sync.aol.com). Device GUID: AFE626E1-58E0-465A-83E4-28D58FE33959. SyncML session DBCDBBFB88654ED38246ABD27843E13A. 0 contact changes — contacts already synchronized. VoIP SIP adapter registered: number 16178766111 (617 area code = Boston/Cambridge, MA), provider VonCP, device MAC 00:1D:D9:2E:4F:61 (Broadcom). The AIM account 'm57jean' links to M57 Patents company (m57.biz) and the character Jean Tanaka (company bookkeeper/analyst). The Gmail account 'mylady.ixchel@gmail.com' is a personal account also linked to the same residential location. Timezone UTC-7 (Pacific DST or Mountain). Cambridge (617) phone number places the subject in Massachusetts.
devil_advocate: The two devices on the network could belong to different household members, not the same person. The Gmail account mylady.ixchel does not necessarily belong to Jean (m57jean AIM). The PHD Comics browsing suggests graduate student activity, which is common in Cambridge MA — many households include multiple students or researchers. The VoIP adapter could pre-date the current occupant. The 0 contact changes in AIM sync means no new contact activity was occurring at the time of capture — this is consistent with routine background sync, not active malicious use. SUSPICION rather than INTENT because co-location of accounts is established but coordination between them is not.
